item.title: TikToker's Plan To Collect 365 Buttons In 2026 Met With Confusion, Becoming An Iconic Moment For The App
item.description: 365 Buttons refers to a viral series of comments left on a video by TikToker @abbieabbieabbie0 by a user known as Tamara where she writes that she is going to get 365 buttons in 2026, one for each day of the year, because she is afraid of time and wants to be more conscious of it. The comment was made on December 21st, 2025 and went viral over the following weeks as the subject of memes and reactions, as Tamara refused to elaborate to commenters regarding what she was going to do with the button

item.title: Drawing Of An Annoyed Steve Harrington Becomes The Biggest Reaction Meme In The 'Stranger Things' Fandom
item.description: Steve Harrington Drawing or Steve Harrington Car Drawing is a reaction image meme based on a drawing of Steve Harrington from Stranger Things driving the show's main characters in his van with his hand on the side of his head and fingers on his temple, as if annoyed. The drawing is based on a scene from Stranger Things season five, episode two and was created by artist Ayisha Zeba in December 2025. The drawing was popularized as a meme throughout late December 2025 and early January 2026.

item.title: Piper Perry Surrounded Meme Appears At Haifa Derby Soccer Match, Resulting In Controversy In Israel
item.description: Piper Perri Surrounded, also known as the White Couch Meme, refers to a series of object labeled and photoshopped image macros of adult film star Piper Perri sitting on a white couch and five Black men standing behind her. Online, the image is labeled to express willful ignorance of an overwhelming series of problems.

item.title: Charli xcx's Song 'House' Becomes Source For Edits And Memes Online
item.description: I Think I'm Gonna Die in This House are lyrics from the Charli xcx pop song "House," which became the source of memes and edits amid a trend in late 2025 and early 2026. The trend, which uses the song and its lyrics as they appear on screen over footage, began appearing in numerous edits shortly after its release in mid-November 2025, spreading over the following months. item.title: A Chicken Screaming At The Top Of A Tree Has Become 2026's Signifier Of Cringe Content
item.description: Chicken Screaming On Tree or Rooster Screaming is an exploitable series of memes based on an image of a chicken standing at the top of a tree paired with a screaming sound effect, as if the chicken is making the sound. The image of the chicken in the tree started going viral in mid-November 2025 and was paired with the screaming sound in late December of that year. As a meme, the screaming chicken is often attached to the end of clips to denote that the clip is cringeworthy or painful to watch.
